title: Bechet covers his fingers from Paul Whiteman's saxophones
summary: When Whiteman's saxophone section came to hear Bechet at Roseland, he draped a handkerchief over his mouthpiece and hands so they could not see his fingering.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Sidney Bechet: the man, the horn, the legend

blocks.x: And Bechet was funny because -- Paul Whiteman's group, they had heard about Bechet. So they were playing a dance at I think it was the Roseland and they all came over and Duke was playing, like, the intermission band, and all of Paul Whiteman's sax section came over there to hear. They wanted to hear Sidney Bechet.

So they told Sidney Bechet that Paul Whiteman's gang was in there to hear him. So they say what Sidney did was to take a handkerchief out of his pocket and put a part on his mouthpiece and the rest over his fingers so they couldn't see what he was fingering and what notes he was doing or nothing.
